subject: Music Production
title: Stem Mastering for Flexibility
description: A micro-lesson that makes Stem Mastering for Flexibility usable.

hook.text: Traditional mastering works with a single stereo mix file, limiting what the engineer can adjust.

buildup.text: Stem mastering receives separate groups: vocals, drums, bass, and instruments as individual files.

discovery.text: The mastering engineer can adjust the balance between groups without affecting other elements.

twist.text: Some purists argue that stem mastering blurs the line between mixing and mastering too much.

climax.text: Stem mastering is increasingly popular because it gives engineers more control over the final sound.

punchline.text: More stems mean more control at the final stage.

quiz.question: What does stem mastering offer that stereo mastering does not?
options: The ability to adjust individual group balances
